chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Utman, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abd Allah informed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who publicizes to us something from our affairs, he is like the one who killed us deliberately, and did not kill us erroneously.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of publicizing the affairs of the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the concept of 'al-ghaybah' (occultation) and the preservation of the Imam's authority by distinguishing between the public and private spheres of their governance. By equating the public disclosure of their secrets to deliberate murder, the Imam highlights that such an act is a calculated attack on their spiritual and political identity, carrying greater weight than an accidental oversight. This principle reinforces the careful curation of information to maintain the distinctiveness of the Imamate against external scrutiny.
